error_history.problem_topic: External Determinism & Denial of Protagonist Moral Agency
error_history.concept: Aristotelian Tragic Flaw (Hamartia): Volitional Agency vs External Catalysts
error_history.type: Absolution of Moral Agency (Conflating External Temptation with Compulsion)
error_history.details: Absolved Macbeth of moral agency. In dramatic theory, external catalysts (the witches, Lady Macbeth) merely illuminate and tempt the protagonist's latent flaw ('vaulting ambition'). Without volitional choice and complicity, the work becomes a tale of mere victimization rather than a tragedy.
